overview: Today's bpf-next activity was dominated by two major patch series. Kumar Kartikeya Dwivedi posted a 9-patch v2 series adding __arena and __arena_nullable argument annotation support to kfuncs and struct_ops, along with corresponding x86 JIT rebasing and trampoline fixes. Pu Lehui continued refining cross-architecture bpf_jit_free fixes (now at v3), addressing memory leaks and a double-free on RO headers across arm64, s390, parisc, sparc64, ARC, and RISC-V JITs, while Leon Hwang submitted a two-patch fix for an incorrect sleepable check in tracing programs.

patches.title: bpf: Support __arena and __arena_nullable kfunc argument suffixes
patches.author: Kumar Kartikeya Dwivedi
patches.summary: This patch introduces support for __arena and __arena_nullable tag suffixes on kfunc pointer arguments in the BPF verifier. When a kfunc argument is annotated with __arena, the verifier ensures the pointer originates from a BPF arena and performs the necessary offset rebasing before the call. The __arena_nullable variant additionally allows a NULL pointer to be passed. This enables kfuncs to safely receive arena-backed pointers with full verifier-enforced provenance, opening the door to more expressive kfunc APIs that operate on arena memory.

patches.title: bpf: Support __arena and __arena_nullable on struct_ops arguments
patches.author: Kumar Kartikeya Dwivedi
patches.summary: Extending the arena argument support from kfuncs to struct_ops, this patch teaches the verifier to recognize __arena and __arena_nullable annotations on struct_ops method arguments. Struct_ops programs can now pass arena-backed pointers through their registered callbacks with the same safety guarantees as kfuncs. This is a prerequisite for struct_ops implementations that manage arena memory and need to expose it via their callback interfaces.

patches.title: bpf, x86: JIT __arena kfunc argument rebasing
patches.author: Kumar Kartikeya Dwivedi
patches.summary: This patch implements the x86-64 JIT changes needed to rebase arena pointer arguments before kfunc calls. When a kfunc is called with an __arena-annotated argument, the JIT must add the arena's base address to the BPF pointer value so the kernel-side kfunc receives a valid virtual address. The patch adds code generation for the rebasing sequence and handles the case where the base is stored in a register to avoid repeated memory loads.

patches.title: bpf: Extract the bpf_jit_binary_hdr helper
patches.author: Pu Lehui
patches.summary: This foundational patch in the bpf_jit_free cleanup series extracts a new bpf_jit_binary_hdr() helper that recovers the JIT binary header from a compiled BPF function pointer. Currently each architecture duplicates this pointer arithmetic inline, leading to divergent implementations and bugs when accounting for CFI or private stack offsets. Centralising the logic in a helper makes subsequent per-architecture leak and double-free fixes simpler and more consistent.

patches.title: bpf: Fix double-free RO header in bpf_jit_free
patches.author: Pu Lehui
patches.summary: The final patch in the v3 bpf_jit_free series fixes a double-free of the read-only (RO) JIT header that occurs when bpf_jit_free is called on a program whose RO header has already been freed by an earlier error path. The bug can be triggered when JIT compilation partially succeeds before failing, leaving the RO header in a freed state while the main prog struct still holds a pointer to it. The fix tracks header ownership correctly so bpf_jit_free only frees the RO header once.

patches.title: bpf: Fix sleepable check for tracing prog
patches.author: Leon Hwang
patches.summary: This patch corrects a logic error in the verifier's sleepable classification for tracing programs. The existing check incorrectly allowed certain tracing programs to be marked sleepable when they attach to non-sleepable kernel functions, potentially enabling blocking operations in contexts where they are not safe. The fix tightens the check to reject such programs at load time, with a companion selftest patch verifying that the corrected rejection is enforced.
